```{r fig.width = figures_height_rmd_output, fig.height = (figures_height_rmd_output * 0.7)}
# --- PLOT ORIGINAL DATA MEAN ± 95 % CI - ONE PLOT FOR EACH SIZE --- #

for(trophy_i in 1:length(trophy_selected)) {
  
  print(trophy_selected[trophy_i])
  
  print(fixed_label)
  plot.ecos.sizes.one.by.one.means(ds_ecosystems,
                                   trophy_selected = trophy_selected[trophy_i],
                                   disturbance_percentage_selected = "fixed",
                                   response_variable_selected)
  
  print(relative_label)
  plot.ecos.sizes.one.by.one.means(ds_ecosystems,
                                   trophy_selected = trophy_selected[trophy_i],
                                   disturbance_percentage_selected = "decreasing_with_size",
                                   response_variable_selected)
  }
```

```{r}

# --- PREPARE DATA FOR ANALYSIS --- #

# Add baselines

baseline = ds_ecosystems %>%
  filter(time_point == time_point_of_baselines) %>%
  select(ecosystem_ID,
         all_of(response_variable_selected)) %>%
  rename(baseline = all_of(response_variable_selected))

data_for_analysis = ds_ecosystems %>%
  left_join(baseline)

# Filter and mutate

data_for_analysis = data_for_analysis %>%
  filter(time_point %in% time_points_model,
         !is.na(!!sym(response_variable_selected))) %>%
  mutate(trophic_type = as.factor(trophic_type),
         size = as.factor(ecosystem_size_ml),
         conn = factor(x = ifelse(connection == "connected", 
                                  "con", 
                                  "unconnected"),
                       levels = c("unconnected", "con")),
         disturbance_percentage = as.factor(disturbance_percentage),
         day = as.double(day),
         ecosystem_ID = as.factor(ecosystem_ID))
```

<details>
<summary>Filtered data mean ± 95 % CI</summary>
```{r fig.width = figures_height_rmd_output, fig.height = figures_height_rmd_output}

# --- PLOT DATA FOR ANALYSIS MEAN ± 95 % CI --- #

plot.ecos.multi.plots(data_for_analysis)
```
</details>
